docs.text: I recommend it - just don’t go in the winter, being on a peninsula jutting into Lake Superior means they get lake effect no matter how the wind blows, and it’s too low for doppler radar to pick up beyond the mountains so you never know what you’ll find 🙃

What it is saying is that the traditional lake effect storm areas including the south shore of Lake Superior and eastern U.P. are going to get hammered. But I am as far upwind on Lake Michigan as you get and too far south of the Lake Superior lake effect snow. Only large storms/blizzards affect us.

Yep most of the west coast of the lower peninsula can get it pretty good from strong west and NW winds. I'm tucked away upwind so don't get much lake effect snow either here unless something strong is pushing down from Lake Superior usually.

Yup…your upstate neighbors in west Michigan are gonna get snowed on every day from now until at least the end of the 8-day forecast. Lake Michigan breaks up some of the worst storms in summer, but she makes us pay for it…it’s a protection racket! 😁

Here on the northwest corner of Lake Michigan, we are too far south for most Lake Superior lake effect to affect us, and don't get much Lake Michigan lake effect unless the weather is coming out of the east/southeast.

The snow is gone and now kids are playing basketball in the park across the street. This is on the south shore of Lake Superior, and normally the conditions are wintry this time of year. In the forecast? Rain.
Morning commutes could be slippery & visibility reduced, especially in along central Lake Superior coast. WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY until 7P ET in Alger County for lake effect snow 3-5" & gusts >35MPH.

Steady rain will taper off from west to east this evening into tonight. Marquette, Green Lake, Fond du Lack, Sheboygan, and northern Washington and Ozaukee Counties stand the best chances for seeing additional snow accumulations. #wiwx #swiwx
Anywhere along Lake Superior, expect heavy snowfall thanks to lake enhancement/lake effect bands. Strong winds will also reduce visibility and make roads very tough to drive on through Sunday night.
LOL Just heard a U.P. (Upper Michigan) weatherman refer to the upcoming weather and lake-effect snow from Lake Superior as, "Mother Superior will be redecorating."
